I like the idea of a subverse for debates - but I feel that having formal debates, at least in our current form with so few active members, would be exceedingly difficult.

Instead, I propose that we start off with the easy thing: We set up a motion once every week, and allow people to freely discuss the motion in the comments.

The time-frame allowed for the debate will be a week. After a week, the moderator will lock the thread, and no more comment may be made.

There are several awards for the best debaters, chosen by upvotes.

These will include:

Best Opening Statement: Awarded to the post with the highest points in the comments. Must be a direct response to the motion (i.e., cannot be a rebuttal to other comments by other posters)

Best Rebuttal: Awarded to the post with the highest points in the comments. Must be a response to a comment.

Best Research: Moderator awarded. Given to whoever has the most sources for their arguments.

As time moves on, and as we get more subscribers, it might be feasible to implement timed debates, or even real time debates organized through IIRC or other channels.

But for now, I think them most realistic thing to do would be to simply set up a motion a week and see where everything goes.

Chinese scientists mull power station in space

Sounds like a pretty difficult engineering problem to solve. Let alone the difficulty of getting something up into space, and transmitting power wirelessly, you have the complexities of collecting power from a source that's moving in relation to the earth.

For example, the station couldn't be in geostationary orbit because China has no territory that intersects with the equator, and you'd still have the problem of not being able to collect day and night.

The article says it would be in geosynchronous orbit, which means you could be in sunlight either at all times or most of the time, but now you have to collect power from something that's moving in relation to the earth. If you transmitted microwaves you'd need to do so directionally because you couldn't just beam things "straight down". That point would be constantly moving and you'd burn a nice figure-eight into the ground, probably thousands of kilometres across.

Sounds like chest-thumping to me, we haven't even figured out wireless power transmission on earth yet. And that's between two point fixed in relation to each other...

If they are seriously considering it we'll soon see when they start devoting funding to microwave power transmission tests on earth long before designs for a space location. If they start making traction in that area then people will start taking it seriously.
